   988→// runExplainCommit explains a specific commit.
   989→func runExplainCommit(w io.Writer, commitRef string) error {
   990→	repo, err := openRepository()
   991→	if err != nil {
   992→		return fmt.Errorf("not a git repository: %w", err)
   993→	}
   994→
   995→	// Resolve the commit reference
   996→	hash, err := repo.ResolveRevision(plumbing.Revision(commitRef))
   997→	if err != nil {
   998→		return fmt.Errorf("commit not found: %s", commitRef)
   999→	}
  1000→
  1001→	commit, err := repo.CommitObject(*hash)
  1002→	if err != nil {
  1003→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to get commit: %w", err)
  1004→	}
  1005→
  1006→	// Get files changed in this commit (diff from parent to current)
  1007→	var files []string
  1008→	commitTree, err := commit.Tree()
  1009→	if err == nil && commit.NumParents() > 0 {
  1010→		parent, parentErr := commit.Parent(0)
  1011→		if parentErr == nil {
  1012→			parentTree, treeErr := parent.Tree()
  1013→			if treeErr == nil {
  1014→				// Diff from parent to current commit to show what changed
  1015→				changes, diffErr := parentTree.Diff(commitTree)
  1016→				if diffErr == nil {
  1017→					for _, change := range changes {
  1018→						name := change.To.Name
  1019→						if name == "" {
  1020→							name = change.From.Name
  1021→						}
  1022→						files = append(files, name)
  1023→					}
  1024→				}
  1025→			}
  1026→		}
  1027→	}
  1028→
  1029→	// Check for Entire metadata - try multiple trailer types
  1030→	metadataDir, hasMetadata := trailers.ParseMetadata(commit.Message)
  1031→	sessionID, hasSession := trailers.ParseSession(commit.Message)
  1032→	checkpointID, hasCheckpoint := trailers.ParseCheckpoint(commit.Message)
  1033→
  1034→	// If no session trailer, try to extract from metadata path.
  1035→	// Note: extractSessionIDFromMetadata is defined in rewind.go as it's used
  1036→	// by both the rewind and explain commands for parsing metadata paths.
  1037→	if !hasSession && hasMetadata {
  1038→		sessionID = extractSessionIDFromMetadata(metadataDir)
  1039→		hasSession = sessionID != ""
  1040→	}
  1041→
  1042→	// Build commit info
  1043→	fullSHA := hash.String()
  1044→	shortSHA := fullSHA
  1045→	if len(fullSHA) >= 7 {
  1046→		shortSHA = fullSHA[:7]
  1047→	}
  1048→
  1049→	info := &commitInfo{
  1050→		SHA:       fullSHA,
  1051→		ShortSHA:  shortSHA,
  1052→		Message:   strings.Split(commit.Message, "\n")[0], // First line only
  1053→		Author:    commit.Author.Name,
  1054→		Email:     commit.Author.Email,
  1055→		Date:      commit.Author.When,
  1056→		Files:     files,
  1057→		HasEntire: hasMetadata || hasSession || hasCheckpoint,
  1058→		SessionID: sessionID,
  1059→	}
  1060→
  1061→	// If we have a checkpoint ID but no session, try to look up session from metadata
  1062→	if hasCheckpoint && sessionID == "" {
  1063→		if result, err := checkpoint.NewGitStore(repo).ReadCommitted(context.Background(), checkpointID); err == nil && result != nil {
  1064→			info.SessionID = result.Metadata.SessionID
  1065→		}
  1066→	}
  1067→
  1068→	// Format and output
  1069→	output := formatCommitInfo(info)
  1070→	fmt.Fprint(w, output)
  1071→
  1072→	return nil
  1073→}
  1074→
  1075→// formatSessionInfo formats session information for display.
  1076→func formatSessionInfo(session *strategy.Session, sourceRef string, checkpoints []checkpointDetail) string {
  1077→	var sb strings.Builder
  1078→
  1079→	// Session header
  1080→	fmt.Fprintf(&sb, "Session: %s\n", session.ID)
  1081→	fmt.Fprintf(&sb, "Strategy: %s\n", session.Strategy)
  1082→
  1083→	if !session.StartTime.IsZero() {
  1084→		fmt.Fprintf(&sb, "Started: %s\n", session.StartTime.Format("2006-01-02 15:04:05"))
  1085→	}
  1086→
  1087→	if sourceRef != "" {
  1088→		fmt.Fprintf(&sb, "Source Ref: %s\n", sourceRef)
  1089→	}
  1090→
  1091→	fmt.Fprintf(&sb, "Checkpoints: %d\n", len(checkpoints))
  1092→
  1093→	// Checkpoint details
  1094→	for _, cp := range checkpoints {
  1095→		sb.WriteString("\n")
  1096→
  1097→		// Checkpoint header
  1098→		taskMarker := ""
  1099→		if cp.IsTaskCheckpoint {
  1100→			taskMarker = " [Task]"
  1101→		}
  1102→		fmt.Fprintf(&sb, "─── Checkpoint %d [%s] %s%s ───\n",
  1103→			cp.Index, cp.ShortID, cp.Timestamp.Format("2006-01-02 15:04"), taskMarker)
  1104→		sb.WriteString("\n")
  1105→
  1106→		// Display all interactions in this checkpoint
  1107→		for i, inter := range cp.Interactions {
  1108→			// For multiple interactions, add a sub-header
  1109→			if len(cp.Interactions) > 1 {
  1110→				fmt.Fprintf(&sb, "### Interaction %d\n\n", i+1)
  1111→			}
  1112→
  1113→			// Prompt section
  1114→			if inter.Prompt != "" {
  1115→				sb.WriteString("## Prompt\n\n")
  1116→				sb.WriteString(inter.Prompt)
  1117→				sb.WriteString("\n\n")
  1118→			}
  1119→
  1120→			// Response section
  1121→			if len(inter.Responses) > 0 {
  1122→				sb.WriteString("## Responses\n\n")
  1123→				sb.WriteString(strings.Join(inter.Responses, "\n\n"))
  1124→				sb.WriteString("\n\n")
  1125→			}
  1126→
  1127→			// Files modified for this interaction
  1128→			if len(inter.Files) > 0 {
  1129→				fmt.Fprintf(&sb, "Files Modified (%d):\n", len(inter.Files))
  1130→				for _, file := range inter.Files {
  1131→					fmt.Fprintf(&sb, "  - %s\n", file)
  1132→				}
  1133→				sb.WriteString("\n")
  1134→			}
  1135→		}
  1136→
  1137→		// If no interactions, show message and/or files
  1138→		if len(cp.Interactions) == 0 {

  1192→// outputWithPager outputs content through a pager if stdout is a terminal and content is long.
  1193→func outputWithPager(w io.Writer, content string) {
  1194→	// Check if we're writing to stdout and it's a terminal
  1195→	if f, ok := w.(*os.File); ok && f == os.Stdout && term.IsTerminal(int(f.Fd())) {
  1196→		// Get terminal height
  1197→		_, height, err := term.GetSize(int(f.Fd()))
  1198→		if err != nil {
  1199→			height = 24 // Default fallback
  1200→		}
  1201→
  1202→		// Count lines in content
  1203→		lineCount := strings.Count(content, "\n")
  1204→
  1205→		// Use pager if content exceeds terminal height
  1206→		if lineCount > height-2 {
  1207→			pager := os.Getenv("PAGER")
  1208→			if pager == "" {
  1209→				pager = "less"
  1210→			}
  1211→
  1212→			cmd := exec.CommandContext(context.Background(), pager) //nolint:gosec // pager from env is expected
  1213→			cmd.Stdin = strings.NewReader(content)
  1214→			cmd.Stdout = f
  1215→			cmd.Stderr = os.Stderr
  1216→
  1217→			if err := cmd.Run(); err != nil {
  1218→				// Fallback to direct output if pager fails
  1219→				fmt.Fprint(w, content)
  1220→			}
  1221→			return
  1222→		}
  1223→	}
  1224→
  1225→	// Direct output for non-terminal or short content
  1226→	fmt.Fprint(w, content)
  1227→}

  1230→const (
  1231→	// maxIntentDisplayLength is the maximum length for intent text before truncation
  1232→	maxIntentDisplayLength = 80
  1233→	// maxMessageDisplayLength is the maximum length for checkpoint messages before truncation
  1234→	maxMessageDisplayLength = 80
  1235→	// maxPromptDisplayLength is the maximum length for session prompts before truncation
  1236→	maxPromptDisplayLength = 60
  1237→	// checkpointIDDisplayLength is the number of characters to show from checkpoint IDs
  1238→	checkpointIDDisplayLength = 12

  1241→// formatBranchCheckpoints formats checkpoint information for a branch.
  1242→// Groups commits by checkpoint ID and shows the prompt for each checkpoint.
  1243→func formatBranchCheckpoints(branchName string, points []strategy.RewindPoint) string {
  1244→	var sb strings.Builder
  1245→
  1246→	// Branch header
  1247→	fmt.Fprintf(&sb, "Branch: %s\n", branchName)
  1248→
  1249→	if len(points) == 0 {
  1250→		sb.WriteString("Checkpoints: 0\n")
  1251→		sb.WriteString("\nNo checkpoints found on this branch.\n")
  1252→		sb.WriteString("Checkpoints will appear here after you save changes during a Claude session.\n")
  1253→		return sb.String()
  1254→	}
  1255→
  1256→	// Group by checkpoint ID
  1257→	groups := groupByCheckpointID(points)
  1258→
  1259→	fmt.Fprintf(&sb, "Checkpoints: %d\n", len(groups))
  1260→	sb.WriteString("\n")
  1261→
  1262→	// Output each checkpoint group
  1263→	for _, group := range groups {
  1264→		formatCheckpointGroup(&sb, group)
  1265→		sb.WriteString("\n")
  1266→	}
  1267→
  1268→	return sb.String()
  1269→}

  1271→// checkpointGroup represents a group of commits sharing the same checkpoint ID.
  1272→type checkpointGroup struct {
  1273→	checkpointID string
  1274→	prompt       string
  1275→	isTemporary  bool // true if any commit is not logs-only (can be rewound)
  1276→	isTask       bool // true if this is a task checkpoint
  1277→	commits      []commitEntry
  1278→}
  1279→
  1280→// commitEntry represents a single git commit within a checkpoint.
  1281→type commitEntry struct {
  1282→	date    time.Time
  1283→	gitSHA  string // short git SHA
  1284→	message string
  1285→}
  1286→
  1287→// groupByCheckpointID groups rewind points by their checkpoint ID.
  1288→// Returns groups sorted by latest commit timestamp (most recent first).
  1289→func groupByCheckpointID(points []strategy.RewindPoint) []checkpointGroup {
  1290→	if len(points) == 0 {
  1291→		return nil
  1292→	}
  1293→
  1294→	// Build map of checkpoint ID -> group
  1295→	groupMap := make(map[string]*checkpointGroup)
  1296→	var order []string // Track insertion order for stable iteration
  1297→
  1298→	for _, point := range points {
  1299→		// Determine the checkpoint ID to use for grouping
  1300→		cpID := point.CheckpointID.String()
  1301→		if cpID == "" {
  1302→			// Temporary checkpoints: group by session ID to preserve per-session prompts
  1303→			// Use session ID prefix for readability (format: YYYY-MM-DD-uuid)
  1304→			cpID = point.SessionID
  1305→			if cpID == "" {
  1306→				cpID = "temporary" // Fallback if no session ID
  1307→			}
  1308→		}
  1309→
  1310→		group, exists := groupMap[cpID]
  1311→		if !exists {
  1312→			group = &checkpointGroup{
  1313→				checkpointID: cpID,
  1314→				prompt:       point.SessionPrompt,
  1315→				isTemporary:  !point.IsLogsOnly,
  1316→				isTask:       point.IsTaskCheckpoint,
  1317→			}
  1318→			groupMap[cpID] = group
  1319→			order = append(order, cpID)
  1320→		}
  1321→
  1322→		// Short git SHA (7 chars)
  1323→		gitSHA := point.ID
  1324→		if len(gitSHA) > 7 {
  1325→			gitSHA = gitSHA[:7]
  1326→		}
  1327→
  1328→		group.commits = append(group.commits, commitEntry{
  1329→			date:    point.Date,
  1330→			gitSHA:  gitSHA,
  1331→			message: point.Message,
  1332→		})
  1333→
  1334→		// Update flags - if any commit is temporary/task, the group is too
  1335→		if !point.IsLogsOnly {
  1336→			group.isTemporary = true
  1337→		}
  1338→		if point.IsTaskCheckpoint {
  1339→			group.isTask = true
  1340→		}
  1341→		// Update prompt if the group's prompt is empty but this point has one
  1342→		if group.prompt == "" && point.SessionPrompt != "" {
  1343→			group.prompt = point.SessionPrompt
  1344→		}
  1345→	}
  1346→
  1347→	// Sort commits within each group by date (most recent first)
  1348→	for _, group := range groupMap {
  1349→		sort.Slice(group.commits, func(i, j int) bool {
  1350→			return group.commits[i].date.After(group.commits[j].date)
  1351→		})
  1352→	}
  1353→
  1354→	// Build result slice in order, then sort by latest commit
  1355→	result := make([]checkpointGroup, 0, len(order))
  1356→	for _, cpID := range order {
  1357→		result = append(result, *groupMap[cpID])
  1358→	}
  1359→
  1360→	// Sort groups by latest commit timestamp (most recent first)
  1361→	sort.Slice(result, func(i, j int) bool {
  1362→		// Each group's commits are already sorted, so first commit is latest
  1363→		if len(result[i].commits) == 0 {
  1364→			return false
  1365→		}
  1366→		if len(result[j].commits) == 0 {
  1367→			return true
  1368→		}
  1369→		return result[i].commits[0].date.After(result[j].commits[0].date)
  1370→	})
  1371→
  1372→	return result
  1373→}

  1375→// formatCheckpointGroup formats a single checkpoint group for display.
  1376→func formatCheckpointGroup(sb *strings.Builder, group checkpointGroup) {
  1377→	// Checkpoint ID (truncated for display)
  1378→	cpID := group.checkpointID
  1379→	if len(cpID) > checkpointIDDisplayLength {
  1380→		cpID = cpID[:checkpointIDDisplayLength]
  1381→	}
  1382→
  1383→	// Build status indicators
  1384→	// Skip [temporary] indicator when cpID is already "temporary" to avoid redundancy
  1385→	var indicators []string
  1386→	if group.isTask {
  1387→		indicators = append(indicators, "[task]")
  1388→	}
  1389→	if group.isTemporary && cpID != "temporary" {
  1390→		indicators = append(indicators, "[temporary]")
  1391→	}
  1392→
  1393→	indicatorStr := ""
  1394→	if len(indicators) > 0 {
  1395→		indicatorStr = " " + strings.Join(indicators, " ")
  1396→	}
  1397→
  1398→	// Prompt (truncated)
  1399→	var promptStr string
  1400→	if group.prompt == "" {
  1401→		promptStr = "(no prompt)"
  1402→	} else {
  1403→		// Quote actual prompts
  1404→		promptStr = fmt.Sprintf("%q", strategy.TruncateDescription(group.prompt, maxPromptDisplayLength))
  1405→	}
  1406→
  1407→	// Checkpoint header: [checkpoint_id] [indicators] prompt
  1408→	fmt.Fprintf(sb, "[%s]%s %s\n", cpID, indicatorStr, promptStr)
  1409→
  1410→	// List commits under this checkpoint
  1411→	for _, commit := range group.commits {
  1412→		// Format: "  MM-DD HH:MM (git_sha) message"
  1413→		dateTimeStr := commit.date.Format("01-02 15:04")
  1414→		message := strategy.TruncateDescription(commit.message, maxMessageDisplayLength)
  1415→		fmt.Fprintf(sb, "  %s (%s) %s\n", dateTimeStr, commit.gitSHA, message)
  1416→	}
  1417→}

  1419→// hasCodeChanges returns true if the commit has changes to non-metadata files.
  1420→// Used by getBranchCheckpoints to filter out metadata-only temporary checkpoints.
  1421→// Returns false only if the commit has a parent AND only modified .entire/ metadata files.
  1422→//
  1423→// First commits (no parent) are always considered to have code changes since they
  1424→// capture the working copy state at session start - real uncommitted work.
  1425→//
  1426→// This filters out periodic transcript saves that don't change code.
  1427→func hasCodeChanges(commit *object.Commit) bool {
  1428→	// First commit on shadow branch captures working copy state - always meaningful
  1429→	if commit.NumParents() == 0 {
  1430→		return true
  1431→	}
  1432→
  1433→	parent, err := commit.Parent(0)
  1434→	if err != nil {
  1435→		return true // Can't check, assume meaningful
  1436→	}
  1437→
  1438→	commitTree, err := commit.Tree()
  1439→	if err != nil {
  1440→		return true
  1441→	}
  1442→
  1443→	parentTree, err := parent.Tree()
  1444→	if err != nil {
  1445→		return true
  1446→	}
  1447→
  1448→	changes, err := parentTree.Diff(commitTree)
  1449→	if err != nil {
  1450→		return true
  1451→	}
  1452→
  1453→	// Check if any non-metadata file was changed
  1454→	for _, change := range changes {
  1455→		name := change.To.Name
  1456→		if name == "" {
  1457→			name = change.From.Name
  1458→		}
  1459→		// Skip .entire/ metadata files
  1460→		if !strings.HasPrefix(name, ".entire/") {
  1461→			return true
  1462→		}
  1463→	}
  1464→
  1465→	return false
  1466→}

Refactor to extract shared transcript types into a new `transcript` package.

**Context:**
PR review feedback identified type duplication between `cmd/entire/cli/types.go` and `cmd/entire/cli/summarise/summarise.go`. Both define: `TranscriptLine`, `userMessage`, `assistantMessage`, `contentBlock`, `toolInput`.

**Tasks:**

1. Create new package `cmd/entire/cli/transcript/`

2. Move/consolidate these types to the new package (export them):
   - `TranscriptLine` (the JSON line structure)
   - `UserMessage` (was `userMessage`)
   - `AssistantMessage` (was `assistantMessage`) 
   - `ContentBlock` (was `contentBlock`)
   - `ToolInput` (was `toolInput`)
   - Related constants: `TypeUser`, `TypeAssistant`, `ContentTypeText`, `ContentTypeToolUse`

3. Update `cmd/entire/cli/types.go` to import from the new package instead of defining locally

4. Update `cmd/entire/cli/summarise/summarise.go` to import from the new package and remove duplicated types

5. Update any other files that reference these types

6. Also fix this issue in `cmd/entire/cli/explain.go` around line 242-256:
   - Remove redundant `[:checkpointIDDisplayLength]` slicing on `checkpointID.String()` calls
   - CheckpointID.String() already returns exactly 12 characters

7. Run `mise run fmt && mise run lint && mise run test` to verify

**Important:**
- Keep the package focused on transcript data structures
- Export types that need to be shared (capitalize first letter)
- Don't move parsing logic yet - just the types
- Preserve all JSON tags

The user is asking how we would use the Generator interface in explain.go instead of directly instantiating ClaudeGenerator. This is about interface-based design in Go.

Currently in explain.go we have:
```go
generator := &summarise.ClaudeGenerator{}
```

To use the interface, we would do:
```go
var generator summarise.Generator = &summarise.ClaudeGenerator{}
summary, err := generator.Generate(ctx, input)
```

Or accept it as a parameter/use dependency injection.

The point is that in Go, interfaces are implicitly satisfied - ClaudeGenerator already implements Generator because it has the `Generate` method with the right signature. We don't need to do anything special.

1. **Initial Context (from summary)**: 
   - Working on ENT-108: AI summaries for checkpoints using Claude CLI
   - Already implemented core functionality: Summary types, summarise package, ClaudeGenerator, --generate and --force flags
   - Just merged from alex/ent-109-text-output-checkpoint-flag branch
   - Task #10 (refactor to separate package) was completed

2. **Large Transcript Discussion**:
   - User asked about handling large transcripts
   - Discussed options: hierarchical summarization, progressive reduction, incremental summarization
   - User noted even 1M context just pushes the problem out
   - Decided to leave for future, create Linear issue

3. **Model Configuration**:
   - Added Sonnet model as default for summarization
   - Added `DefaultModel = "sonnet"` constant and `Model` field to ClaudeGenerator
   - Created Linear issue ENT-141 for large transcript handling
   - User reminded to link ENT-141 to ENT-108

4. **PR Review Comments (First Round)**:
   - Type duplication in summarise.go - User chose option B: create transcript package
   - Used subagent to extract shared types to cmd/entire/cli/transcript/

5. **PR Review Comments (Second Round - Current)**:
   - Multiple comments from Copilot and cursor[bot]:
     1. Missing nil check after reload (Medium) - FIXED
     2. Missing MarkFlagsMutuallyExclusive - Already present after merge
     3. Misleading comment about truncation - Comment is correct, no change
     4. extractUserContentFromMessage duplication - FIXED (moved to transcript package)
     5. parseTranscriptFromBytes duplication - FIXED (moved to transcript package)
     6. Unused Generator interface - User chose option A: use interface type in explain.go

6. **Fixes Made**:
   - Added nil check after reloading checkpoint result
   - Changed `generator := &summarise.ClaudeGenerator{}` to `var generator summarise.Generator = &summarise.ClaudeGenerator{}`
   - Created transcript/parse.go with ParseFromBytes and ExtractUserContent
   - Updated summarise/summarise.go to use transcript package functions
   - Updated cli/transcript.go to use transcript package functions
   - Removed unused imports (bufio, bytes, io from summarise.go; bytes from transcript.go)
   - Fixed wrapcheck lint errors by wrapping errors from transcript package

7. **Commits Made**:
   - "fix: address PR review feedback" (ee8003a)

8. **Replied to Review Comments**:
   - Replied to 3 Copilot comments explaining fixes or why no change needed

Summary:
1. Primary Request and Intent:
   - Implement ENT-108: AI-powered checkpoint summaries using Claude CLI
   - Address PR review comments on the implementation
   - The user wanted to discuss and address the latest round of review comments
   - User specifically asked how to use the Generator interface (option A: use interface type)
   - User requested replies to the review comments after fixes were committed

2. Key Technical Concepts:
   - Claude CLI integration with `--model sonnet` for cost-effective summarization
   - Generator interface pattern for extensibility and testing
   - Shared transcript package for type and function deduplication
   - Error wrapping for lint compliance (wrapcheck)
   - Nil checks after reloading data that can return (nil, nil)
   - Interface-based dependency design in Go

3. Files and Code Sections:
   - **cmd/entire/cli/transcript/parse.go** (NEW)
     - Created to eliminate code duplication between cli and summarise packages
     - Contains shared parsing functions
     ```go
     // ParseFromBytes parses transcript content from a byte slice.
     func ParseFromBytes(content []byte) ([]Line, error) {
         var lines []Line
         reader := bufio.NewReader(bytes.NewReader(content))
         // ... parsing logic
         return lines, nil
     }

     // ExtractUserContent extracts user content from a raw message.
     func ExtractUserContent(message json.RawMessage) string {
         var msg UserMessage
         if err := json.Unmarshal(message, &msg); err != nil {
             return ""
         }
         // ... extraction logic with textutil.StripIDEContextTags
         return ""
     }
     ```

   - **cmd/entire/cli/explain.go**
     - Added nil check after reloading checkpoint (line 234-237)
     - Changed to use Generator interface type (line 279)
     ```go
     // Reload the result to get the updated summary
     result, err = store.ReadCommitted(context.Background(), fullCheckpointID)
     if err != nil {
         return fmt.Errorf("failed to reload checkpoint: %w", err)
     }
     if result == nil {
         return fmt.Errorf("checkpoint not found after save: %s", fullCheckpointID)
     }
     
     // Generate summary using Claude CLI
     var generator summarise.Generator = &summarise.ClaudeGenerator{}
     ```

   - **cmd/entire/cli/summarise/summarise.go**
     - Removed duplicated parseTranscriptFromBytes function
     - Removed duplicated extractUserContentFromMessage function
     - Updated to use transcript package
     ```go
     import (
         "context"
         "encoding/json"
         "fmt"
         "strings"
         "entire.io/cli/cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint"
         "entire.io/cli/cmd/entire/cli/transcript"

         lines, err := transcript.ParseFromBytes(content)

         }
         return BuildCondensedTranscript(lines), nil
     }

     func extractUserEntry(line TranscriptLine) *Entry {
         content := transcript.ExtractUserContent(line.Message)
         // ...
     }
     ```

   - **cmd/entire/cli/transcript.go**
     - Updated to use shared functions, removed bytes import
     ```go
     func parseTranscriptFromBytes(content []byte) ([]transcriptLine, error) {
         lines, err := transcript.ParseFromBytes(content)
         if err != nil {
             return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to parse transcript: %w", err)
         }
         return lines, nil
     }

     func extractUserContentFromMessage(message json.RawMessage) string {
         return transcript.ExtractUserContent(message)
     }
     ```

+	Generate(ctx context.Context, input Input) (*checkpoint.Summary, error)

+	EntryTypeTool EntryType = "tool"

+type Entry struct {
+	// Type is the entry type (user, assistant, tool)
+	Type EntryType
+

+	Content string
+
+	// ToolName is the name of the tool (for tool entries)
+	ToolName string
+
+	// ToolDetail is a description or file path (for tool entries)
+	ToolDetail string
+}
+
+// TranscriptLine is an alias to the shared transcript.Line type.
+type TranscriptLine = transcript.Line
+
+// BuildCondensedTranscriptFromBytes parses transcript bytes and extracts a condensed view.
+// This is a convenience function that combines parsing and condensing.
+func BuildCondensedTranscriptFromBytes(content []byte) ([]Entry, error) {
+	lines, err := parseTranscriptFromBytes(content)
+	if err != nil {
+		return nil, err
+	}
+	return BuildCondensedTranscript(lines), nil
+}
+
+// parseTranscriptFromBytes parses transcript content from a byte slice.
+// Uses bufio.Reader to handle arbitrarily long lines.
+func parseTranscriptFromBytes(content []byte) ([]TranscriptLine, error) {
+	var lines []TranscriptLine
+	reader := bufio.NewReader(bytes.NewReader(content))
+
+	for {
+		lineBytes, err := reader.ReadBytes('\n')
+		if err != nil && err != io.EOF {
+			return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to read transcript: %w", err)
+		}
+
+		// Handle empty line or EOF without content
+		if len(lineBytes) == 0 {
+			if err == io.EOF {
+				break
+			}
+			continue
+		}
+
+		var line TranscriptLine
+		if err := json.Unmarshal(lineBytes, &line); err == nil {
+			lines = append(lines, line)
+		}
+
+		if err == io.EOF {
+			break
+		}
+	}
+
+	return lines, nil

    58→type TranscriptLine = transcript.Line
    59→
    60→// BuildCondensedTranscriptFromBytes parses transcript bytes and extracts a condensed view.
    61→// This is a convenience function that combines parsing and condensing.
    62→func BuildCondensedTranscriptFromBytes(content []byte) ([]Entry, error) {
    63→	lines, err := transcript.ParseFromBytes(content)
    64→	if err != nil {
    65→		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to parse transcript: %w", err)

    67→	return BuildCondensedTranscript(lines), nil
    68→}
    69→
    70→// BuildCondensedTranscript extracts a condensed view of the transcript.
    71→// It processes user prompts, assistant responses, and tool calls into
    72→// a simplified format suitable for LLM summarisation.
    73→func BuildCondensedTranscript(lines []TranscriptLine) []Entry {
    74→	var entries []Entry
    75→
    76→	for _, line := range lines {
    77→		switch line.Type {
    78→		case transcript.TypeUser:
    79→			if entry := extractUserEntry(line); entry != nil {
    80→				entries = append(entries, *entry)
    81→			}
    82→		case transcript.TypeAssistant:

    84→			entries = append(entries, assistantEntries...)
    85→		}
    86→	}
    87→

    89→}

    92→// Returns nil if the line doesn't contain a valid user prompt.
    93→func extractUserEntry(line TranscriptLine) *Entry {
    94→	content := transcript.ExtractUserContent(line.Message)
    95→	if content == "" {
    96→		return nil
    97→	}
    98→	return &Entry{
    99→		Type:    EntryTypeUser,
   100→		Content: content,
   101→	}
   102→}
   103→
   104→// extractAssistantEntries extracts assistant and tool entries from a transcript line.
   105→func extractAssistantEntries(line TranscriptLine) []Entry {
   106→	var msg transcript.AssistantMessage
   107→	if err := json.Unmarshal(line.Message, &msg); err != nil {
   108→		return nil
   109→	}
   110→
   111→	var entries []Entry
   112→
   113→	for _, block := range msg.Content {
   114→		switch block.Type {
   115→		case transcript.ContentTypeText:
   116→			if block.Text != "" {
   117→				entries = append(entries, Entry{
   118→					Type:    EntryTypeAssistant,
   119→					Content: block.Text,
   120→				})
   121→			}
   122→		case transcript.ContentTypeToolUse:
   123→			var input transcript.ToolInput
   124→			_ = json.Unmarshal(block.Input, &input) //nolint:errcheck // Best-effort parsing
   125→
   126→			detail := input.Description
   127→			if detail == "" {
   128→				detail = input.Command
   129→			}
   130→			if detail == "" {
   131→				detail = input.FilePath
   132→			}
   133→			if detail == "" {
   134→				detail = input.NotebookPath
   135→			}
   136→			if detail == "" {
   137→				detail = input.Pattern
   138→			}
   139→
   140→			entries = append(entries, Entry{
   141→				Type:       EntryTypeTool,
   142→				ToolName:   block.Name,
   143→				ToolDetail: detail,
   144→			})
   145→		}
   146→	}
   147→
   148→	return entries
   149→}
   150→
   151→// FormatCondensedTranscript formats an Input into a human-readable string for LLM.
   152→// The format is:
   153→//
   154→//	[User] user prompt here
   155→//
   156→//	[Assistant] assistant response here
   157→//
   158→//	[Tool] ToolName: description or file path
   159→func FormatCondensedTranscript(input Input) string {
   160→	var sb strings.Builder
   161→
   162→	for i, entry := range input.Transcript {
   163→		if i > 0 {
   164→			sb.WriteString("\n")
   165→		}
   166→
   167→		switch entry.Type {
   168→		case EntryTypeUser:
   169→			sb.WriteString("[User] ")
   170→			sb.WriteString(entry.Content)
   171→			sb.WriteString("\n")
   172→		case EntryTypeAssistant:
   173→			sb.WriteString("[Assistant] ")
   174→			sb.WriteString(entry.Content)
   175→			sb.WriteString("\n")
   176→		case EntryTypeTool:
   177→			sb.WriteString("[Tool] ")
   178→			sb.WriteString(entry.ToolName)
   179→			if entry.ToolDetail != "" {
   180→				sb.WriteString(": ")
   181→				sb.WriteString(entry.ToolDetail)
   182→			}
   183→			sb.WriteString("\n")
   184→		}
   185→	}
   186→
   187→	if len(input.FilesTouched) > 0 {
   188→		sb.WriteString("\n[Files Modified]\n")
   189→		for _, file := range input.FilesTouched {
   190→			fmt.Fprintf(&sb, "- %s\n", file)
   191→		}
   192→	}
   193→
   194→	return sb.String()
   195→}
